title: The Grace of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The grace of God is His undeserved favor freely given to sinners through Jesus Christ. Grace gives what people cannot earn, deserve, purchase, or produce by their own righteousness.
summary: The grace of God is His undeserved favor freely given to sinners through Jesus Christ. Grace gives what people cannot earn, deserve, purchase, or produce by their own righteousness.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the fullest gift of God’s grace. Through His life, death, and resurrection, sinners receive forgiveness, righteousness, new life, and eternal hope by grace.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Grace is not God rewarding human worthiness. It is God’s free and saving favor toward the undeserving. Sinners do not bring merit to God; they receive mercy and life because God is gracious.

The grace of God is revealed supremely in Christ. The Word became flesh, full of grace and truth. Through Him, sinners are justified freely, not because they have earned righteousness, but because God gives salvation through redemption in Christ.

Grace not only saves; it trains. Scripture teaches that grace instructs believers to deny ungodliness and live soberly, righteously, and godly. Grace is never permission to remain in sin; it is power and favor that lead to holiness.

God’s grace was given according to His purpose before time and revealed through the appearing of Christ. The believer’s hope rests not on human effort, but on the saving grace of God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people swing between pride and despair. Pride says, 'I can earn this.' Despair says, 'I am too far gone.' Grace answers both by placing salvation entirely in God’s generous favor through Christ.

This doctrine protects the Gospel from becoming self-help or religious performance. It tells the broken that they may come empty-handed, and it tells the proud that they must.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive grace as a gift, not a wage. Stop trying to prove your worthiness before God, and stop assuming your failure is stronger than Christ. Let grace humble you, restore you, train you, and move you toward grateful obedience.
